criteria.rationale: The naming assumes Git always prints top-relative names, which diff.relative changes. L1 was read and is not disputed.
The delta adds one read-only rev-parse and no shared state; the concurrent index-read test is in the focused run, which passed.
No schema or tool contract changes; at the repository top names are unchanged because the prefix is empty.
Revisions stay validated and a failed untracked listing fails with its cause. The silent prefix fallback is low, in N2.
The report warning carries the Git message and a test now requires it.
Nothing differs at the top; a lower root with diff.relative selects less than before.
Naming after the diff, instead of filtering with --relative, addresses the cause of R2-N1, but depends on an output form the command does not fix. The design assessment observed no structural deltas.
Examined the amended requirements, execution log and follow-up: they match behaviour for the shipped CLI. Leftover wording is N3 and N5.
Selection errors and the report warning name the failing read and what Git said.
R1 to R5 as amended each have a passing focused test; N1 concerns the scope selection fix, which no requirement states.
The nine code files match the spec artifact list; the lower-root selection change answers earlier findings and is stated in the spec API section and log.
Changed names, including ../ forms, are only matched as strings in the code read, never opened; the versioned report interpolates nothing from Git.
A prefix lookup and a small rename function is proportionate; it holds only while the diff output form is fixed, the condition N1 breaks.

findings.action: Regression: the diff does not pin diff.relative, and the new naming assumes top-relative output. With the root below the top and diff.relative=true in Git config, a change to proj/mod/x.txt is named ../mod/x.txt and the self-contained module that owns it is not selected, with no error; the base engine selected it (reproduced against both versions). In that configuration a tracked change outside the root is also still dropped, changed=[], as at base. Validation narrows silently. Reach: only a root below the repository top, which the shipped CLI does not pass (it resolves the top).

scopeRootPrefix trims all surrounding space, so below a directory with a leading space every change is named as outside and its self-contained module is not selected (reproduced; base did not select it either). By reading, a failing rev-parse also returns an empty prefix silently, which restores the R1-N7 misnaming.

An outside change is named ../ plus its top-relative name, which is root-relative only for a root one level down. With root a/b, a/c/f.txt becomes ../a/c/f.txt, so a self-contained module declaring ../c is not selected (reproduced; base did not select it either). The spec API section says names are relative to the root and records no decision on this outside form.

Pre-existing: ls-files runs under the root, so below the top a new untracked file outside the root is not listed and nothing is selected for it (reproduced, same at base), unlike a tracked outside change.
Rest of R2-N3: report.go:314-317 still describes a bounded line with absolute paths removed, and the comment at validate_index_residuals_test.go:134 still says the report bounds its note.
